title: La surveillance est votre raison d'être [Invitation]

description.main: An invitation card for Barbara Kruger's exhibition of recent work, Œuvres récentes, at Galerie Crousel-Hussenot in Paris, 16 May to 19 June 1984, headed La surveillance est votre raison d'être.
description.extended:
An invitation card for Barbara Kruger's exhibition of recent work, Œuvres récentes, at Galerie Crousel-Hussenot in Paris, 16 May to 19 June 1984, headed La surveillance est votre raison d'être.

The show is the first of two Kruger exhibitions in the gallery's archive; the second followed in 1987. Kruger showed regularly with Crousel-Hussenot between 1984 and 1987. The Larousse dictionary of painting cites Sans titre (La surveillance est votre raison d'être), 1984, as an example of how her reworked advertising images question economic values, social relations and the roles of men and women. Her works of these years use large photographs taken from illustrations and advertisements, often framed in red.
description.artist_bio: Barbara Kruger (b. 1945, Newark) is an American conceptual artist associated with the Pictures Generation. After working as a designer and picture editor at Conde Nast magazines, she began in the late 1970s to pair found black-and-white photographs with declarative text in Futura Bold Oblique, white on red. The Barbara Kruger Catalogue Raisonne (barbarakruger.org) documents the work; she is represented by Sprueth Magers and David Zwirner.
description.exhibition_context: Galerie Chantal Crousel's online archive lists a Barbara Kruger exhibition in spring 1984 and a second in February and March 1987.

notes: Invitation card, Galerie Crousel-Hussenot, Paris. The card gives the dates 16 May to 19 June 1984; Galerie Chantal Crousel's online archive lists the show as 19 April to 16 May 1984. Larousse (Dictionnaire de la peinture) dates the work Sans titre (La surveillance est votre raison d'être) to 1984.
